section: Amendment of the Constitution - Article 368, types of majorities, procedure, limitations
subsections: Special majority - different meanings across Articles 368, 249, 312, 61

accepted.s: Which one of the following correctly describes the majority required under the Article 368 type of special majority?
o: Majority of the total membership of each House and two-thirds of the members present and voting in each House
Two-thirds of the total membership of each House
Two-thirds of the members present and voting in the Rajya Sabha only
Simple majority of the total membership of both Houses taken together
accepted.x: The Article 368 type requires both a majority of the total membership of each House and a two-thirds majority of members present and voting in each House.
accepted.tq: Separate the total-membership requirement from the present-and-voting requirement.
accepted.sec: Special majority - different meanings across Articles 368, 249, 312, 61  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The majority required for the impeachment of the President of India is
o: Two-thirds of the total membership of the House concerned
Two-thirds of the members present and voting in both Houses
Majority of the total membership and two-thirds of members present and voting in both Houses
Three-fourths of the total membership of Parliament
accepted.x: Under the Article 61 type of majority, impeachment of the President requires two-thirds of the total membership of the House concerned.
accepted.tq: Watch for the distinction between total membership and members present and voting.
accepted.sec: Special majority - different meanings across Articles 368, 249, 312, 61  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Match List-I with List-II and select the correct answer using the code given below:

List-I (Provision)
A. Article 368 type of majority
B. Article 61 type of majority
C. Article 249
D. Article 312

List-II (Subject)
1. Impeachment of the President
2. Creation of new All-India Services
3. Constitutional amendment
4. Parliament's power to legislate on a State List subject

Codes:
A B C D
accepted.x: Article 368 type relates to constitutional amendment; Article 61 type to presidential impeachment; Article 249 to legislation on a State List subject; and Article 312 to new All-India Services.
accepted.tq: Start with the sure pair and eliminate codes that misplace the constitutional provision.
accepted.sec: Special majority - different meanings across Articles 368, 249, 312, 61  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following is NOT correctly matched?
o: Article 61 type majority — Impeachment of the President
Article 249 type majority — Creation of a new All-India Service
Article 368 type majority — Approval of a National Emergency
Article 368 type majority — Removal of a Comptroller and Auditor-General
accepted.x: Creation of a new All-India Service under Article 312 requires the Article 249/312 type of majority in the Rajya Sabha, not the Article 368 type of majority.
accepted.tq: Find the provision whose majority has been swapped with a neighbouring category.
accepted.sec: Special majority - different meanings across Articles 368, 249, 312, 61  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Article 368 type of special majority is relevant to which one of the following sets of provisions?
accepted.x: The Article 368 type of majority is used for removal of Supreme Court and High Court judges, the CAG, the CEC and State Election Commissioners, constitutional amendment, and approval of a National Emergency. The relevant provisions include Articles 124, 217, 148, 324, 243K and 352.
accepted.tq: Use the provision-number cluster to distinguish the Article 368 category from Articles 249, 312 and 61.
accepted.sec: Special majority - different meanings across Articles 368, 249, 312, 61  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: A proposal to authorise Parliament to legislate on a matter in the State List is passed by a two-thirds majority of the members present and voting in the Rajya Sabha. This majority is of the type associated with
o: Article 61 only
Articles 249 and 312
Article 368 only
Articles 124 and 217
accepted.x: The two-thirds-of-members-present-and-voting requirement in the Rajya Sabha is the Article 249/312 type. It applies both to Article 249 resolutions and to the creation of new All-India Services under Article 312.
accepted.tq: Identify the constitutional provision from the House and voting threshold described in the scenario.
accepted.sec: Special majority - different meanings across Articles 368, 249, 312, 61  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements:
1. The Constitution of India combines rigidity and flexibility in its amendment procedure.
2. The basic-structure limitation permits judicial review of constitutional amendments.
3. Every provision of the Constitution can be amended by a simple majority of Parliament.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1 and 3 only
2 and 3 only
1, 2 and 3
accepted.x: Statements 1 and 2 are correct. Statement 3 is false: only certain provisions can be altered through the simple-majority route, while other provisions require special procedures and are subject to the basic-structure limitation.
accepted.tq: Reject the absolute claim that all constitutional provisions follow one amendment route.
accepted.sec: Special majority - different meanings across Articles 368, 249, 312, 61  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following was the latest enacted Constitutional Amendment as indicated for 2023?
o: 106th Amendment
104th Amendment
107th Amendment
105th Amendment
accepted.x: The 106th Constitutional Amendment, enacted in 2023, is identified as the latest enacted amendment in the stated reference period.
accepted.tq: Distinguish an enacted amendment from later amendment Bills that remain under consideration.
accepted.sec: Special majority - different meanings across Articles 368, 249, 312, 61  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, which proposed fast-tracking women's reservation, was defeated in the Lok Sabha after receiving
o: 230 votes for and 298 votes against out of 528 members present and voting
298 votes for and 230 votes against out of 528 members present and voting
298 votes for and 230 votes against out of 550 members present and voting
300 votes for and 228 votes against out of 528 members present and voting
accepted.x: The Bill proposed increasing Lok Sabha strength from 550 to 850 and was defeated with 298 votes in favour and 230 against among 528 members present and voting.
accepted.tq: Check the vote total and the direction of the for-and-against figures before applying the majority test.
accepted.sec: Special majority - different meanings across Articles 368, 249, 312, 61  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Consider the following statements regarding constitutional amendment proposals referred to in 2026:
1. The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, relating to women's reservation and delimitation, was negatived in the Lok Sabha.
2. The Delimitation Bill, 2026, was withdrawn.
3. The Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024, relating to simultaneous elections, was before a Joint Parliamentary Committee.
4. The Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2026, concerns removal of a Prime Minister, Chief Minister or Minister detained for 30 consecutive days for an offence punishable with five or more years of imprisonment.
Which of the statements given above are correct?
o: 1 and 2 only
1, 2 and 3 only
2, 3 and 4 only
accepted.x: All four statements are correct. The 131st Bill concerned women's reservation and delimitation, the Delimitation Bill was withdrawn, the 129th Bill was before a JPC, and the 130th Bill addressed continued detention of specified ministers for serious offences.
accepted.tq: Separate the subject and procedural status of each numbered Bill instead of treating all amendment proposals alike.
accepted.sec: Special majority - different meanings across Articles 368, 249, 312, 61  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s:
Arrange the following in chronological order of their identification or introduction:
A. Constitution (106th Amendment) enacted
B. Constitution (129th Amendment) Bill, 2024
C. Constitution (130th Amendment) Bill, 2026
D. Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026
o: A, B, C, D
B, A, C, D
A, C, B, D
B, C, D, A
accepted.x: The 106th Amendment was enacted in 2023, followed by the 129th Amendment Bill in 2024, and then the 130th and 131st Bills in 2026.
accepted.tq: Fix the 2023 and 2024 entries first, then order the two 2026 proposals.
accepted.sec: Special majority - different meanings across Articles 368, 249, 312, 61  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: The Constitution (131st Amendment) Bill, 2026, failed to secure the required two-thirds support among members present and voting primarily because
o: the Bill was required to be passed unanimously by both Houses
the number voting against was more than two-thirds of the total Lok Sabha membership
the Rajya Sabha rejected it by a two-thirds majority
the number voting in favour was 298 out of 528, which was less than two-thirds
accepted.x: Two-thirds of 528 is 352, whereas the Bill received only 298 votes in favour. It was negatived in the Lok Sabha; the stated vote was not a Rajya Sabha vote or a unanimity requirement.
accepted.tq: Apply the present-and-voting threshold numerically rather than comparing the result with total House strength.
accepted.sec: Special majority - different meanings across Articles 368, 249, 312, 61  [GROUP-II]

accepted.s: Which one of the following best reflects the criticism and constitutional significance associated with the 2026 vote on the proposed amendment?
o: It established that a simple majority is always sufficient for constitutional amendment, although critics favour greater executive power.
It demonstrated that the basic structure can be altered whenever both Houses agree by a simple majority.
It showed that every constitutional amendment must be approved by a referendum, although critics oppose judicial review.
It showed that a special majority can protect constitutional change from being secured by a slim majority, although critics consider simple-majority routes too easy.
accepted.x: The vote was viewed as demonstrating the protective role of a special majority against a slim majority. At the same time, critics argue that routes using only a simple majority make constitutional change too easy.
accepted.tq: Match the two linked ideas—protection through special majority and criticism of easy simple-majority routes.
accepted.sec: Special majority - different meanings across Articles 368, 249, 312, 61  [GROUP-II]
